I've been working this land for 50 years now, so I don't think too hard about it — I mostly do what worked last year. My 7 mu is split the same way every year: wheat in winter, maize in summer, rotating on the same ground. Three mouths at home, so I need both crops to come in steady.

For the winter wheat, I'll plant an improved variety — Jimai or something similar that the seed shop sells. I learned years ago the hybrid maize and improved wheat give better yields than the old seeds my father used. For wheat I put down about 2 bags of compound fertilizer (diammonium) before sowing as base fertilizer, then topdress with urea at jointing in spring. That comes out to around 16 kg of nitrogen per mu total, maybe 7 kg phosphorus, 5 kg potassium. If I put too little, I lose yield and that's a disaster. A little extra fertilizer is just some extra yuan — I'd rather spend it.

Well water is close so I irrigate the wheat 3 times: before winter, at green-up in spring, and at grain filling. Spray once for aphids and once for rust if I see it. Plough before sowing wheat — the soil needs turning after maize stubble.

Summer maize I plant right after wheat harvest in June, no time to waste. Hybrid seed — Zhengdan or Denghai, whatever the dealer has that neighbors trust. Rotary till through the stubble, direct seed. About 18 kg N per mu (base plus one topdressing at big trumpet stage), 6 kg P, 5 kg K. Irrigate twice if rain is short — usually at tasseling and grain filling. Spray once for borer.

Wheat I expect around 450 kg per mu, maize around 550 kg per mu. That's what I got last year and the year before. Weather decides the rest.
